correctness.rationale: Exact first-moment and covariance-by-derivative identities are derived from finite Bernoulli products. Degree-sum leaf compensation proves positivity below 1/3, direct degree signs prove negativity beyond 1/2, and exact second derivative with a strict global bound on g_d establishes concavity and a unique zero in between. Path and star roots attain sharp limiting endpoints. The K15-plus-two-path cyclic graph shows at least three derivative roots using certified rational values at four rational points. Exact independent site-configuration enumerations verify 141 small-tree covariance identities, not the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: A topology-independent strict probability interval and unique sign switch quantify the transition between growing occupancy and isolation-fragmentation counts for any tree-shaped habitat network; paths and stars prove the limits are optimal over all tree sizes. An explicit connected graph with cycles has three changes, documenting a substantive sharp graph-class limitation. The structural result is not a numerical optimization or a restatement of the degree polynomial; it proves global strict uniqueness by a leaf-surplus argument.
